`budget.py` now takes an optional `YYYY-MM` argument and counts only that month's transactions; with no argument it behaves exactly as before. I ran it against your data:

| Envelope | No month (all transactions) | `2026-08` | `2026-09` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 403.05 | 371.55 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 78.10 | 124.75 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 111.50 | 84.25 |
| household | 54.61 | 73.01 | 101.60 |

- **Empty months:** a month with no transactions (e.g. `2026-10`) shows every envelope at its full allocation rather than an error.
- **Bad input:** anything that isn't a valid `YYYY-MM` (`sept`, `2026-9`, `2026-13`) or any extra argument prints a message to stderr and exits with status 2.
